name: jira-flow
description: ACTIVATE THIS PLUGIN whenever the user's message contains a Jira ticket key ({PREFIX}-{NUMBER}, e.g. ABC-1234) or an Atlassian issue URL (https://<site>.atlassian.net/browse/KEY-123) -- ALWAYS, with NO exception for extra content in the same message. A ticket key or URL activates this plugin whether it stands alone OR is accompanied by screenshots, images, pasted bug descriptions, annotations like 'image 1 = wrong, image 2 = correct', requirements, or any other text. That accompanying material is NOT a separate task to investigate directly -- it is additional context for Step 1 of the jira-pull workflow (folded into the ticket summary and the Step 3 scope confirmation), and the full branch-setup/questions/transition workflow still runs before any code is touched. Do not interpret a URL plus a bug description plus screenshots as 'the user wants me to go investigate/fix this now' -- that exact shape (URL + description + before/after images) is the most common real input and still means 'start working on this ticket' via the full workflow, not 'skip the workflow and start debugging'. Also activate on 'start ticket', 'jira-pull', 'jira-push', 'jira-create', 'create ticket', 'new ticket', 'file bug', 'close ticket', 'wrap up', 'done with this ticket', 'create an MR/PR'. Provides the complete Jira ticket lifecycle: creating standardized tickets with active sprint/backlog placement ('jira-create'), starting a ticket with branch setup, sprint check, scope, time estimate ('jira-pull'), and closing a ticket with pre-push checks, commit, push, MR/PR, Jira transition, worklog ('jira-push'). MANDATORY NEXT STEP: immediately after activating this plugin, load and follow the skill instructions for 'jira-create', 'jira-pull', or 'jira-push' BEFORE any other action (view the corresponding skills/*/SKILL.md file or invoke the skill) -- including fetching or creating the Jira ticket, searching the codebase, or writing code.
